# A template can be named without ever being parsed into. template.New
# puts an entry in the set straight away, so a lookup of that name finds
# a template whose tree is still nil, and everything downstream has to
# expect one.
#
# Here the set is rooted at "base" but no base.gohtml is embedded, so
# "base" is named and never filled in.
#
# Nothing is reported for it. Executing it would fail at run time with an
# incomplete template, which this tool does not diagnose yet, but it has
# to say so rather than crash, and the templates around it still check.

check-templates -v
stdout 'index\.gohtml'
! stderr .

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.25.0
-- main.go --
package main

import (
	"embed"
	"fmt"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var source embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.New("base").ParseFS(source, "*"))

type Page struct {
	Title string
}

func render() {
	_ = templates.ExecuteTemplate(io.Discard, "base", Page{Title: "Home"})
	_ = templates.ExecuteTemplate(io.Discard, "index.gohtml", Page{Title: "Home"})
}

var _ = fmt.Sprint

-- index.gohtml --
<h1>{{.Title}}</h1>
